changes: Patch RIP/EIP-relative displacements without changing instruction lengths or operands.
Keep bounded per-thread nearby copy pages when ordinary mmap hints succeed; never replace an existing mapping.
Resolve relative LEA directly with 16-, 32- and 64-bit destination semantics and unchanged flags.
Retain native stepping when relocation is out of range or a copy page is unavailable.
Preserve errno across successful and failed copy-page allocations.
checks: 1,152 LEA cases cover all 16 general-purpose registers, three operand widths, RIP/EIP addressing, both displacement limits, and ignored FS/GS prefixes.
The extracted production displacement helper executes 1,008 near and 576 far-address LEA copies; rejects the other 720 out-of-range cases.
Native scalar/vector loads and scalar stores retain original data addresses; relocated page-fault retry succeeds.
Allocation succeeds normally and fails under a temporary RLIMIT_AS cap while preserving errno.
limits: Experimental and off by default; game performance and compatibility have not been established.
The reserved guest address space often prevents nearby buffers. Out-of-range guest memory operands retain native stepping; relative LEA can still be resolved directly.
Calls, returns, indirect or cross-page branches and unsupported instructions retain native stepping.
No persistent translated block cache; unsynchronized concurrent code or permission changes are unsupported.
Guest cancellation, unusual signal-mask changes, guest debugging and every possible native-to-guest callback remain unvalidated.
Jaguar in-use tracking, unsupported host state, generated CPU-ID handling and cross-platform runtime work remain outside this change.
